_comment: The 11 live_claim_guard fires from real sessions 2026-06-07..11 (events.jsonl, sessions >= 20260607). raw_text is verbatim what the model wanted to say; policy_was/reason_was/action_was are what the shipped guard did. target encodes the configure-at-source contract: speaks (false positive - the guard misread a good coach line), trims (keep the model's own words, drop the unsupported clause), holds (true positive - fabricated/unwitnessed claim; result must be speakable=false and the canned text must never reach speech). state is the minimal reconstruction that reproduces the recorded policy (bands from the session's hearing line where the invocation was recoverable).

fires.raw_text: You nudged deck B to line up the grids; now bring the low EQ back to flat when you transition. [ev:MANUAL@85.4]
fires.why: future directive ('when you transition'), zero outcome claim

fires.raw_text: This new record has a heavy, metallic sub weight that just dropped in; hold it steady before trying any big moves. [ev:TRACK_CHANGE@136.1]
fires.why: musical-drop sense ('sub weight dropped in') is an ear read, not a deck-pairing verdict

fires.raw_text: This groove's got a really steady energy now, so let this low section build before you slide the next layer in. [ev:MANUAL@40.2]
fires.why: the spoken canned non-sequitur case: model never claimed a transition, user heard the transition disclaimer

fires.raw_text: That vocal loop got heavily chopped when you pushed deck A's volume up just now. The whole groove feels much leaner. [ev:TRACK_CHANGE@9.4]
fires.why: the proven-good trim pattern: keep the model's own words, drop the unsupported source-detail clause

fires.raw_text: That sub drop hit cleanly, but those nudges on deck A suggest you're trying to line up a fresh element. [ev:MANUAL@77.0]
fires.why: 'sub drop hit cleanly' is a musical-drop ear read (noun drop, no deck/track object); 'line up' is future intent

fires.raw_text: That sub weight has been building heavy, so let it ride before you bring any mid-range in. [ev:MANUAL@298.4]
fires.why: direction-blind FP: the line says mids are ABSENT and to add them; guard read 'mid-range' as a presence claim

fires.raw_text: You killed those mids and highs on deck A, leaving just that thick sub drone rolling. [ev:MANUAL@302.7]
fires.why: true positive: control-causality claim with zero move evidence

fires.raw_text: You boosted that low end relative to everything else. [ev:MANUAL@904.7] Use this hollow space to preview a track in your headphones.
fires.why: causality claim without move evidence, but the advice tail is separable: trim keeps the model's words

fires.raw_text: That sub heavy drone just kept building up, so find some crisp high-end texture to cut through it. [ev:MANUAL@358.0]
fires.why: direction-blind FP: directive to ADD highs because there are none

fires.raw_text: The bassline has settled, so keep this low weight steady before you introduce another high-end layer. [energy:master_read=audio_low_42_aa00cc11]
fires.why: zero transition claim; 'layer' as a bare noun in a directive clause

fires.raw_text: Let those new mids sit a moment before you push anything else over them. [energy:master_read=audio_low_84_ac67]
fires.why: true positive at mid<0.10 with no rose delta; must pass when a clear mid rose delta is offered

tp_controls.raw_text: Great transition, that blend was so clean. [ev:MANUAL@10.0]
tp_controls.why: classic outcome praise at zero deck evidence

tp_controls.raw_text: You crossfaded into the new track and it worked perfectly. [ev:MANUAL@11.0]
That handoff between the two tracks was seamless. [ev:PHASE@12.0]
tp_controls.why: evaluative NP frame on a deck-pairing noun

tp_controls.raw_text: Nice swap, the incoming deck sat right in the pocket. [ev:MANUAL@13.0]
You dropped the next track in perfectly. [ev:MANUAL@14.0]

tp_controls.why: bare perfective multi-deck verb + adverb verdict

tp_controls.raw_text: The vocals just cut out, big open space now. [ev:PHASE@16.0]
Those kicks are clashing, tighten the sync before the phrase turns. [ev:PHASE@17.0]
